S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Combined Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development across multiple settings (e.g., work, home, social). Symptoms must have been present since childhood, although adults may first come to clinical attention when environmental demands exceed their coping strategies, revealing long-standing but previously compensated difficulties. The course is typically chronic, with manifestations evolving over time—hyperactivity may become more subjective restlessness in adults, while organizational and planning difficulties often become more prominent. It is distinguished from mood, anxiety, and personality disorders by its early onset, cross-situational cognitive/behavioral pattern, and the absence of episodic mood changes or primary motivational or comprehension deficits.

patient.personality: Janelle is an energetic, socially outgoing planner who enjoys keeping busy with work, fitness, and community events, often pushing herself with caffeine-fueled enthusiasm.
patient.stressor: Janelle’s challenges intensified when she was promoted from a basic front-desk role to an administrative specialist position in the school district, which required her to manage complex workflows, coordinate multi-departmental meetings, and participate in lengthy committee sessions. The job amplified demands on her ability to wait through structured agendas, listen to others finish before speaking, and manage multiple stakeholders’ needs, all while her social enthusiasm pushed her to volunteer for additional projects and after-hours events. Over the next two years, her tendency to jump into conversations, struggle with orderly turn-taking in meetings, and overcommit to tasks began to create friction with supervisors and colleagues, who perceived her as overly eager and occasionally disruptive despite her strong work ethic. After a tense performance review that highlighted her difficulty staying in her lane during discussions and complaints from coworkers about her interrupting in group settings, she recognized that these patterns were affecting both her advancement and her social relationships and sought psychiatric help to understand what was going on.
patient.chief_complaint: “At work and in meetings I just can’t seem to wait my turn—I jump in before other people are finished and it’s starting to cause problems.”

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: In those long committee meetings, I’ll start out really focused on the agenda, and then twenty minutes in my mind just drifts to what I’m making for dinner or the song stuck in my head, and suddenly I realize I’ve missed a whole chunk of what people decided while I was sitting right there nodding along.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: My coworkers tease me because they’ll give me instructions at my desk, and even though I’m looking right at them, it’s like my brain is somewhere else and I have to say, ‘Sorry, can you repeat that?’ because I honestly didn’t absorb a word.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: I’ll jump into a project at work all excited—like putting together meeting packets or scheduling a whole round of interviews—but then I get sidetracked by emails or someone stopping by, and hours later I realize I never finished the original task and there are half-done forms still sitting on my screen.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: With all the different principals, committees, and events I’m supposed to juggle, I stare at my to-do list and don’t even know where to start, so I end up bouncing between things and then scrambling at the last minute when a deadline suddenly pops back into my awareness.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: Pretty much every morning I’m running around the apartment or the office hunting for my badge, my planner, or whatever folder I swore I just had in my hand, because I set things down in random spots without thinking and then can’t retrace my steps.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: During those long board meetings, I tell myself to stay seated like everyone else, but after a while I get so antsy that I invent reasons to get up—refilling my water, checking the copier—just so I can move around for a minute.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: Once I get going, especially in staff meetings or at after-hours events, I just keep talking and adding comments or stories, and I only realize I’ve been dominating the conversation when I notice people going quiet or glancing at each other.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: In meetings I’ll jump in with my suggestion the second I think of it, finishing people’s sentences or answering questions before my supervisor has even finished asking, and then I see that look on her face like, ‘Can you let me finish first?’

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Whether it’s waiting my turn to speak during a roundtable or standing in line at the copy room, I get really impatient and fidgety, checking the time and almost physically biting my tongue because I feel this urge to just cut in and get it over with.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I have this habit of sliding into other people’s conversations or hovering over their desks to offer ideas while they’re working, and I don’t realize I’ve interrupted or derailed them until they give me a polite but tight smile or later mention they lost their train of thought.
